title: Cost of a job placement: what can and cannot be computed
question: How much does one job placement cost in City-funded workforce programmes?
finding: The data on disk cannot support a cost per job placement over time. Human Rights Commission payments to the Japanese Community Youth Council per Opportunities for All placement: $4,564 in 2025 ($7.2 million for 1,584); one year only, so no trend can be drawn.
how: The only pair of figures on disk that line up is the Human Rights Commission's yearly count of job placements through the Opportunities for All youth programme and its payments to the nonprofit that runs the programme's payroll, the Japanese Community Youth Council. Payments under that department code begin in fiscal year 2025. City money is taken from the Controller's nonprofit-spending table, which keeps contracted services only and leaves out other payments to the same organizations.
limits: No trend can be drawn. The workforce office published placements by programme area for fiscal year 2022 only (4,410 people placed out of 7,011 enrolled); its 2023 and 2024 outcome reports are published as pictures with no readable figures, results by provider are not published at all, and the payment data does not separate workforce grants from the office's business and neighbourhood grants. Most of the Opportunities for All money is wages paid to the young people placed, so the figure is not an overhead cost. The placement count is the department's own.

rows.measure: Human Rights Commission payments to the Japanese Community Youth Council per Opportunities for All placement

sources.t: City and County of San Francisco, Controller: Citywide Performance Metrics (open data 6dpt-7w23)
San Francisco Office of Economic and Workforce Development: Workforce Program Outcomes, fiscal year 2021-22
City and County of San Francisco, Controller: nonprofit contracts and spending (open data qkex-vh98)
